slides.heading: Right Sibling Tree
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Binary Trees
slides.narration: Let's solve Right Sibling Tree, a very hard binary trees problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Transform in place so every node's right pointer points to the next node on the same level (null at the end of a level); left pointers keep the first child.
Level-by-level, O(1) extra space using the already-linked level above.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Transform in place so every node's right pointer points to the next node on the same level (null at the end of a level); left pointers keep the first child. Level-by-level, constant extra space using the already-linked level above.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Process top-down: a left child's sibling is the right child, and a right child's sibling is the parent's sibling's left child.
slides.narration: Process top-down: a left child's sibling is the right child, and a right child's sibling is the parent's sibling's left child.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: BFS level order with a queue → O(n) time, O(w) space
Recursive with parent sibling pointers → O(h)
slides.narration: Level-order processing is straightforward and linear. The recursive version uses the parent's new sibling pointer to reach cousins, saving space.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, recurse with parent and side. Second, save the old right child. Third, set right to the sibling. Fourth, recurse on children.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Point every node's right to its right neighbour
slides.narration: Rewire every node so its right pointer points to the next node on the same level.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Process level by level
slides.narration: Gather each level's nodes first, from the old pointers, then rewire right pointers along the level.

lines: children collected before rewiring → no data lost

slides.caption: Collect children before rewiring
slides.narration: Collecting the next level before overwriting right pointers is what keeps the right children reachable.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We build each next level from the current level's children, then set each node's right to the following node in the level.

slides.heading: Complexity
bullets: Space: O(1) (iterative, besides an original-children snapshot per level)
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant (iterative, besides an original-children snapshot per level).

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Don't lose right children while rewiring
Last node on a level → null
slides.narration: Grab the children before you overwrite right.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Process top-down: a left child's sibling is the right child, and a right child's sibling is the parent's sibling's left child.
